reference.title: API endpoint enhancements
reference.shortdesc: You can review API enhancements in Red Hat Quay 3.18, including robot federation audiences, organization application OAuth token life cycle endpoints, and bootstrap token renewal.

section.title: Robot federation audiences field
section.p: Robot federation configuration entries now support an optional audiences array in addition to issuer and subject. During federated robot token exchange (GET /oauth2/federation/robot/token), when audiences is present on the matching federation entry, Red Hat Quay validates the external OIDC token audience against that list. When audiences is absent, audience validation is skipped and Red Hat Quay logs a deprecation warning advising you to configure audiences.
A future release requires the audiences field for federated robot authentication.

Configure federation entries by using the UI or POST /api/v1/organization/{orgname}/robots/{robot_shortname}/federation. In Red Hat Quay 3.18, create and update requests persist issuer and subject only; audience validation applies when audiences is present in the stored federation configuration. For field descriptions, examples, and current API limitations, see createOrgRobotFederation and Configuring federation audiences.

section.title: Organization application OAuth token life cycle
section.p: Red Hat Quay 3.18 adds REST API endpoints to manage OAuth API tokens for organization applications:
Create requests accept name, scope, and optional expiration (seconds). The bearer token secret is returned only in the create response.
For API schemas and examples, see createOrganizationApplicationToken, listOrganizationApplicationTokens, and deleteOrganizationApplicationToken.

section.title: Bootstrap token renewal
section.p: When FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP is enabled, POST /api/v1/bootstrap/renew rotates the bootstrap OAuth token. The new token is written to the configured filesystem path or Kubernetes Secret, and the previous token is invalidated immediately. The response is {"status": "rotated"}.
For more information, see renewBootstrapToken and Renewing the bootstrap token. The following API endpoints were added in Red Hat Quay 3.18.

section.title: Repository mirror health API endpoints
section.p: New health endpoints report the status of repository mirroring operations, including worker availability, repository sync counts, and detected issues. Both require a fresh login. Global queries without a namespace require superuser access; namespace-scoped queries require organization membership or user-admin permission for that namespace.

entry.p: Return health status for repository mirroring operations. Optional namespace and detailed query parameters. Returns HTTP 200 when healthy and HTTP 503 when unhealthy.
Return a global mirror health summary for superusers without repository-identifying samples. Returns HTTP 200 when healthy and HTTP 503 when unhealthy.

section.p: See getRepositoryMirrorHealth and getSuperUserRepositoryMirrorHealth for more information, including example commands.
